projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Public systems and selected professional work.
projects.professionalNote: Employer-owned system. The source is not public.

clawai.summary: A local-first AI orchestration platform that runs open models on your own machine and routes each prompt to the most suitable one.
clawai.role: Architected and built the platform end to end — microservices backend, orchestration layer and web workspace.
clawai.overview: Claw gives a team one workspace to manage, route, compare and operate many AI models at once. It prioritises private local inference through Ollama and llama.cpp, while still reaching cloud providers when a task needs them, so sensitive prompts can stay on hardware the organisation controls.
clawai.architecture: A NestJS microservices backend sits behind a Next.js workspace, with PostgreSQL for relational data, MongoDB for documents, Redis for caching and queues for background work. A provider abstraction puts local and cloud models behind one interface, which is what makes routing, fallback and comparison possible without special-casing each vendor.
clawai.engineering: The interesting problems were routing and trust: choosing a model per prompt, falling back when a provider degrades, and running comparison, consensus and judge workflows over several answers. Around that sit memory and context packs, workspace grounding, file processing, permission-aware tool execution for connected business tools, provider credential handling and health aggregation.

auraspear.summary: An AI-first, multi-tenant SOC platform unifying SIEM, SOAR and threat intelligence in one investigation workspace.
auraspear.role: Designed and implemented the platform: tenant isolation model, RBAC, investigation workflows and AI-assisted analysis.
auraspear.overview: AuraSpear brings alerts, cases, incidents, hunts, intelligence enrichment and detection engineering into a single governed workspace. It is built for teams that serve several tenants at once, where one customer's data must never be reachable from another's session.
auraspear.architecture: Next.js and NestJS over PostgreSQL with Prisma, Redis for caching, and OpenSearch for log search at volume. Wazuh and MISP feed detections and threat intelligence, and AWS Bedrock backs the AI reasoning. Tenant isolation is enforced in the data layer rather than the UI, and every connector credential is handled server-side.
auraspear.engineering: The core work was making multi-tenancy and RBAC unavoidable rather than optional — scoping every query, every job and every AI call to a tenant. On top of that sits alert triage, case management, threat hunting, intelligence enrichment, and AI assistance woven into the investigation rather than bolted on beside it.

foodorder.summary: A mobile-first collaborative ordering app where a group shares one order and the cost splits fairly and transparently.
foodorder.role: Built the application end to end: architecture, data model, offline behaviour, bilingual UI and mobile packaging.
foodorder.overview: One person opens a shared bucket, invites others, and everyone adds their own items. When the order closes, each participant sees exactly what they owe, with delivery fees distributed fairly instead of guessed at. It runs as a web app and ships to Android and iOS from the same codebase.
foodorder.architecture: React, TypeScript and Vite, packaged with Capacitor for Android and iOS. Firebase Authentication handles identity and Cloud Firestore stores buckets, invitations and contributions, with its offline persistence letting people keep adding items on a weak connection and reconcile later.
foodorder.engineering: The demanding parts were correctness and fairness: role-scoped collaboration, per-member contributions, immutable order snapshots at closing time, and receipt and fee distribution that has to be right to the last unit. Full Arabic and English support including RTL was part of the design from the start, not retrofitted, and the flows are covered by cross-browser and mobile tests.

twinzyai.summary: A privacy-focused AI style and vibe game that reads visible traits from a photo without ever identifying anyone.
twinzyai.role: Built the full stack and designed the privacy pipeline that keeps image data out of storage entirely.
twinzyai.overview: Players upload a photo and get a playful reading of their visible style and vibe, which they can share through a temporary link. The whole product is designed around a constraint: it must be fun without becoming a face-recognition tool.
twinzyai.architecture: A Next.js front end with a NestJS and Fastify API, containerised with Docker, calling Gemini for analysis. The pipeline validates the image, extracts visible traits, discards the image buffer immediately, and every stage after that works on text only.
twinzyai.engineering: The privacy properties are the feature: no facial recognition, no identity matching, no image persistence, and text-only processing once traits are extracted. Around that sit secure image validation, safety gates on generated content, expiring share links, bilingual Arabic and English support, and a mobile-first PWA build.

nextranger.summary: A strict Next.js engineering base where architectural decisions are enforced by tooling instead of documented and forgotten.
nextranger.role: Author. Designed the architecture model, the custom ESLint rule set and the quality gates.
nextranger.overview: NextRanger is the starting point I use for serious frontend work. Its premise is that conventions a team agrees to but cannot enforce will erode, so every rule that matters is expressed as a lint rule, a type, or a failing test rather than a paragraph in a README.
nextranger.architecture: Next.js App Router with Server Components by default, strict TypeScript, and a module-first layout with one-way dependencies: routes depend on modules, modules on shared code, shared on vendor wrappers, and never the reverse. Each third-party package has exactly one owning wrapper, so upgrades and error handling live in a single reviewed file.
nextranger.engineering: A custom ESLint plugin enforces the layer policy, package ownership, TSX-only components and translation coverage. Vitest and Playwright cover unit, integration, end-to-end, accessibility and visual testing, alongside internationalisation with RTL, a nonce-based CSP, and CI gates that run the whole set before anything merges.

myoncare.summary: A Class IIa medical device under EU MDR that lets patients share treatment plans, medication and activity data with their healthcare teams.
myoncare.role: Backend and full-stack engineer since 2022, working across care task management, patient monitoring and wearable integrations.
myoncare.overview: myoncare connects patients and care teams around a shared treatment plan: medication schedules, care tasks and activity data flow in one direction, clinical guidance flows back, and both sides see the same up-to-date picture. As a regulated Class IIa medical device, every workflow change has to hold up to EU MDR traceability requirements, not just work correctly.
myoncare.architecture: A NestJS backend fronts a React web app and a React Native and Capacitor mobile app from one shared TypeScript codebase. MySQL holds structured clinical and care-task records; MongoDB holds higher-volume, less structured activity and wearable data. RabbitMQ carries background work — wearable sync jobs, notification fan-out — off the request path, with Redis in front of the read-heavy endpoints. FHIR gives the platform a standard shape for exchanging data with external health systems instead of a bespoke integration per partner.
myoncare.engineering: Built and maintained care task management, patient monitoring dashboards and the wearable integration pipelines that keep activity data current. Containerised every service with Docker so the same image runs identically in staging and production, which matters more than usual under EU MDR change control.

garment-io.summary: A smart-manufacturing platform helping garment factories digitise operations, track production and monitor performance from real-time shop-floor data.
garment-io.role: Backend and full-stack engineer, building operational dashboards and IoT device integrations.
garment-io.overview: Garment IO replaces paper-based shop-floor tracking with a live picture of production: what's being made, on which line, at what rate, and where the bottlenecks actually are — sourced directly from shop-floor devices rather than end-of-shift manual entry.
garment-io.architecture: A Node.js API and a set of PHP/Laravel services split responsibilities by domain, with Python and Flask handling data-processing work that benefited from Python's ecosystem. MongoDB stores the high-frequency device event stream; MySQL holds the structured operational and reporting data. Redis caches the dashboards' read-heavy queries, and Nginx fronts the whole stack.
garment-io.engineering: Built the operational dashboards factory managers use to track production in real time, and the IoT device integrations that feed them — turning raw shop-floor signals into the metrics a factory floor actually acts on.

tarsyaa.summary: A B2B procurement and tender management platform connecting companies with certified suppliers across KSA through transparent, competitive bidding.
tarsyaa.role: Built backend services with strict TypeScript, unit testing and role-based access control for supplier onboarding and bidding workflows.
tarsyaa.overview: Tarsyaa runs the procurement process itself as a product: companies publish tenders, certified suppliers bid, and the whole cycle — onboarding, eligibility, bidding, award — is transparent and auditable instead of happening over email and spreadsheets.
tarsyaa.architecture: A NestJS backend with TypeORM against PostgreSQL, Redis for caching and session-adjacent state, and a Vite-built React frontend. The whole stack is containerised with Docker for consistent environments from local development through to production.
tarsyaa.engineering: Delivered supplier onboarding and bidding workflows behind strict TypeScript and role-based access control, with unit tests covering the eligibility and award logic — the parts of a bidding platform where a quiet bug is a real business problem, not just a UI glitch.

ovarc.summary: A global business-expansion platform streamlining incorporation, payroll, benefits, compliance and international HR operations.
ovarc.role: Contributed full-stack features across the incorporation and HR-operations workflows.
ovarc.overview: Ovarc lets a company expand into a new country without hiring a local HR and legal team for every market: incorporation, payroll, benefits and compliance all run through one platform instead of a different vendor and process per country.
ovarc.architecture: A Node.js backend with a React frontend, using Sequelize and Prisma across different services depending on when each was built — a pragmatic split rather than a planned dual-ORM design, reflecting a platform that grew service by service. MySQL is the system of record throughout, and the whole stack runs in Docker.
ovarc.engineering: Shipped full-stack features across the incorporation and HR-operations workflows, working inside an existing service boundary and data model rather than a greenfield build.

callrater.summary: A call analytics and rating platform for enterprise performance tracking and reporting.
callrater.role: Developed backend data processing and reporting dashboards.
callrater.overview: CallRater turns raw call-centre activity into the metrics a dealership or enterprise team actually manages against: call volume, agent performance and quality ratings, rolled up into reporting rather than left as raw call logs.
callrater.architecture: A PHP backend on Apache with MySQL for storage, and an Angular frontend for the reporting dashboards.
callrater.engineering: Built the backend data-processing pipeline that turns call records into performance metrics, and the reporting dashboards that present them to enterprise teams.

vms.summary: A volunteering management platform for a GIZ programme, supporting registration, assignment workflows and administrative reporting.
vms.role: Built the platform's business workflows and reporting on Laravel.
vms.overview: Built for a GIZ-run programme, this platform manages the full volunteering lifecycle: registration, matching volunteers to assignments, and the administrative reporting a donor-funded programme needs to demonstrate its own reach.
vms.architecture: A Laravel application using Eloquent against MySQL, served from Apache, with JavaScript handling the interactive parts of the admin and volunteer-facing screens.
vms.engineering: Implemented the registration and assignment workflows end to end, plus the administrative reporting views programme staff use to track participation and outcomes.

health-integrations.summary: Integrations connecting a healthcare platform to external health and wearable data sources.
health-integrations.role: Implemented FHIR, Withings, Apple Health and Android Health Connect integrations for activity and treatment data synchronisation.
health-integrations.overview: A healthcare platform is only as useful as the data reaching it. This work built the integration layer that pulls activity and treatment data in from the wearable and platform health APIs patients actually use, instead of relying on manual entry.
health-integrations.architecture: A Node.js integration layer normalises each source into a FHIR-shaped record before it reaches the rest of the platform, with native Swift and Kotlin hooks on the mobile side for the platform-specific health APIs that have no server-side equivalent.
health-integrations.engineering: Implemented FHIR-based data exchange alongside direct integrations with Withings, Apple Health and Android Health Connect, so activity and treatment data stays in sync regardless of which device or platform a patient uses.

payment-integrations.summary: Payment and platform integrations for production applications.
payment-integrations.role: Implemented Stripe and PayPal payment processing and a Spotify API integration.
payment-integrations.overview: Cross-project payment and third-party platform integration work: wiring production applications to the payment processors and external APIs they depend on, correctly handling the failure and edge cases a payment integration can't afford to get wrong.
payment-integrations.architecture: NestJS and Node.js services on the TypeScript side, PHP services where an existing codebase called for it, integrating Stripe and PayPal for payment processing and the Spotify API for a music-data feature.
payment-integrations.engineering: Implemented Stripe and PayPal payment processing end to end — including the webhook and reconciliation paths that matter as much as the checkout flow itself — and a Spotify API integration for retrieving and processing music metadata.

about.title: About
about.description: Background, approach and how I prefer to work.

paragraphs.one: I am a senior software engineer based in Egypt, working mainly in backend and integration engineering with Node.js, TypeScript and NestJS, and comfortable across the full stack with React and Next.js.
paragraphs.two: Most of my work has been on systems that have to keep running: a Class IIa medical platform under EU MDR, a manufacturing platform fed by real-time shop-floor data, and multi-tenant platforms where isolation between customers is a correctness requirement rather than a feature.
paragraphs.three: I like the parts of the job that happen before and after the code — turning a vague requirement into a concrete design, drawing the boundaries a system will live with for years, and then owning what happens when it is live at three in the morning.
paragraphs.four: I value clean architecture, maintainability and continuous learning, and I try to balance strong engineering standards against what the business actually needs to ship.
